lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Know it, prepare for it, and help each other. Today, we follow the light of the Safety Lantern to the small airport on the Island of Fire. Look at its big white roof. It looks like two huge wings! That's why people call it the Airport of Wings. Birimo opens his map. There's a little wings mark right here! Then a young albatross comes over to us. She wears a blue scarf and a captain's cap. Hello! I'm Skye, the junior guide of this airport. Every trip is a story! She points to the tall windows. Planes are taking off one after another. Skye says, From here, planes leave for every corner of the world. Say it with me. Planes leave for every corner of the world. Great! Ms. Emma smiles and holds up her travel pouch. Your passports are safe in here, she says. We're going on a trip abroad together! Skye gives each of us a small blue book. Let's read the first page. "Welcome to the Wing Stamp Book! This is not a passport. It is a book for your travel story. There are six empty pages inside. Each time you finish one part of your trip, one page will be filled. Use polite words, help your friends, and always stay with your group. When all six pages are full, a big surprise is waiting for you. Have a wonderful trip, and remember, every trip is a story!" How many empty pages are there? Six. Is the Wing Stamp Book a passport? No, it isn't. It's a book for our travel story. Now, phonics. Look at the departures board. We read flight numbers in small parts. Flight 205 is flight two oh five. Zero often sounds like oh. Flight 318 is flight three eighteen. Flight 760 is flight seven sixty. Flight 1120 is flight eleven twenty. Our plane is Flight 205! Next time, we will go to the check-in counter with our bags!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Planes leave for every corner of the world. Today, we pull our suitcases to the check-in counter. There's a short line, so we wait our turn. Then a friendly clerk in a green jacket waves to us. Ms. Emma steps up to the counter with all of us and says, Good morning. I'd like to check in, please. Say it with me. I'd like to check in, please. Great! Before we go on, let's read the sign on the counter. "Welcome to the Check-In Counter. Check-in for Flight 205 opens at 7:15 and closes at 10:00. Please have your passport ready. Put your bags on the scale one at a time. We will put a baggage tag on each bag, so it can find its way to the right plane. Keep medicine and important things in your small bag. After check-in, please go to the security check. Have a wonderful flight!" What time does check-in open? At 7:15. What goes on each bag? A baggage tag. The clerk asks, May I see your passports, please? Ms. Emma takes our passports out of her travel pouch. Here you are. Then the clerk asks, How many bags are you checking? Two bags, please. The bags go on the scale, and the clerk puts a baggage tag on each one. Bye-bye, bags! See you later! Birimo tries to climb onto the scale, too. Oh, Birimo! You're not a bag! Everyone laughs, even the clerk. Now, phonics. Let's read times. Say the hour, and then the minutes. 10:45 is ten forty-five. That's when our plane leaves. 6:05 is six oh five. The zero sounds like oh. 12:30 is twelve thirty. 7:15 is seven fifteen. Listen carefully. Fifteen is strong at the end. Fifty is strong at the beginning. Next time, we will choose our seats. Do you like the window or the aisle?

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I'd like to check in, please. We are still at the check-in counter. Our bags have their tags, and now it's time to choose our seats. The clerk looks at Haru and asks, Would you like a window seat or an aisle seat? Say it with me. Would you like a window seat or an aisle seat? Great! An aisle is the long, narrow path between the seats. Haru doesn't need to think. A window seat, please! I want to see the clouds. Sure. Your seat is 14A. Kiko says, I'd like an aisle seat, please. Then I can stand up and stretch my legs. Riko is happy in the middle, between her two friends. Ms. Emma asks, Can we sit together? The clerk smiles. Of course. You're all in rows 14 and 15. Ms. Emma will sit right behind the children, in 15B. Then the clerk prints our boarding passes. Let's read Haru's boarding pass. "Boarding Pass. Passenger: Haru. Flight: 205. From: the Airport of Wings. To: Skyport International Airport. Gate: 23B. Boarding time: 10:15. Departure time: 10:45. Seat: 14A, window. Seats A and F are next to the windows. Please be at your gate by boarding time. The gate closes fifteen minutes before departure. Keep this boarding pass with your passport until you are on the plane. Thank you, and enjoy your flight!" What is Haru's seat? 14A, a window seat. What time does boarding start? At 10:15. Birimo reads his boarding pass. Seat 15A! A window seat, too! He does a happy little dance. Now, phonics. Seat numbers are a number and a letter. Seat 14A is seat fourteen A. Seat 32F is seat thirty-two F. Seat 8C is seat eight C. Seat 21D is seat twenty-one D. Be careful with fourteen and forty. Fourteen is strong at the end. Forty is strong at the beginning. Next time, we will listen to the airport announcements very carefully!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Excuse me. Do you know where gate 23B is? Today, we are on Flight 205! Haru sits by the window in 14A, Riko is in 14B, and Kiko is on the aisle in 14C. Birimo and Ms. Emma are right behind them. Ding! The seatbelt sign is on, so we fasten our seatbelts. Click! The plane goes faster and faster down the runway, and then we're in the air! Haru's ears feel strange. Ms. Emma says, Try yawning or chewing. That helps. Soon a kind flight attendant comes down the aisle with a cart. Kiko is thirsty, so she asks, Could I have some water, please? Say it with me. Could I have some water, please? Great! The flight attendant smiles. Of course. Here you are. Riko feels a little cold. Could I have a blanket, please? Then the pilot makes an announcement. Let's read it. "Good afternoon, everyone. This is your captain speaking. Welcome aboard Flight 205. We are now flying high above the sea. The weather is clear, and the visibility is excellent, so please look out of your window. You can see small green islands below. In a few minutes, our flight attendants will serve drinks and a light lunch. When the seatbelt sign is on, please stay in your seat with your seatbelt fastened. Thank you, and enjoy the flight!" What can we see out of the window? Small green islands. What will the flight attendants serve? Drinks and a light lunch. Now, phonics. Vis means see. Vision means how well you can see. Birds like Skye have amazing vision. Visibility means how far you can see. On a foggy day, the visibility is poor. Visual means about seeing. The safety card is very visual. It has pictures, so you can understand it with your eyes. Next time, we will land in a new country and meet a passport officer!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Could I have some water, please? After a long flight, we land at Skyport International Airport. It's huge! There are moving walkways, bright signs, and travelers from all over the world. Ms. Emma says, Stay together, everyone. First, we go to passport control. Let's read the sign on the wall. "Welcome to Skyport International Airport. All visitors, please go to Passport Control. Have your passport ready. Families may go to the officer together, and children should stay with their adult. The officer will check your passport and may ask you a few simple questions, for example, why you are visiting and how long you will stay. After that, collect your bags and go through Customs. Enjoy your stay!" What should children do? Stay with their adult. Where do you go after passport control? To Customs. Now it's our turn. We walk up to the desk together. A friendly officer smiles at us. Hello! What's the purpose of your visit? Ms. Emma answers, Sightseeing. Say it with me. What's the purpose of your visit? Sightseeing. Great! Purpose means reason. Sightseeing means visiting famous and beautiful places. The officer asks, How long will you stay? For five days. Where are you staying? At the Seagull Hotel in Brightwater. Then the officer looks at Kiko and asks, Is this your first visit? Kiko answers, Yes, it is! The officer laughs and says, Welcome! Have a wonderful time! Now, phonics. Vis means see. Visit means to go and see a person or a place. A visitor is a person who comes to see a place. A visa is a paper or stamp that lets you enter a country. Some countries need a visa, and some don't. When you want a good idea from someone who knows a place, you can say, Could you recommend a good restaurant? To recommend something means to say, This one is good. You should try it! Haru tries it. Excuse me. Could you recommend a good restaurant? Say it with me. Could you recommend a good restaurant? Great! Mr. Lee smiles and asks, What kind of food do you like? Riko says, We love fish! Mr. Lee says, Then how about the Little Anchor? It's a fish restaurant by the river. He gives us a page from the hotel's city guide. Let's read the guide. "The Little Anchor. This small family restaurant sits right by the river, near the old stone bridge. The fish comes fresh from the harbor every morning. Try the grilled fish with lemon, or the famous fish soup. lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Could you recommend a good restaurant? Today, we are practicing all our hotel English. Birimo says, I'm playing Mr. Lee! Welcome to the Seagull Hotel! We take turns. Haru checks in with his reservation. Riko asks for an extra pillow. Kiko asks where the nearest station is. Then, oh no! Dark clouds are rolling in, and it starts to rain. We want to walk to the River Market with Ms. Emma, but we don't have umbrellas. Ms. Emma says, Many hotels lend umbrellas to guests. Let's ask politely. Kiko goes to the front desk with Ms. Emma and says, I'd like to borrow an umbrella. Could you lend me one? Say it with me. I'd like to borrow an umbrella. Could you lend me one? Super! Borrow means you take something and give it back later. Lend means you give something, and it comes back to you. Mr. Lee points to a sign. Let's read the sign. "Rainy Day? We can help! Seagull Hotel guests may borrow umbrellas from the front desk for free. Large umbrellas are blue, and small umbrellas for children are yellow. Please write your room number on the list when you borrow one. If you need a raincoat, just ask. Bring the umbrellas back to the front desk before you check out. Enjoy Brightwater, rain or shine!" What color are the children's umbrellas? Yellow. When do we bring them back? Before we check out. Then Skye lands by the door, shaking rain from her wings. She says, Every trip is a story, and today's story is about kind words! She opens the Wing Stamp Book and presses our third stamp onto the page. Now, phonics. Let's review. lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I'd like to borrow an umbrella. Could you lend me one? This morning, Ms. Emma sits down with us in the lobby. She says, I have something to tell you. On the day we arrived, my suitcase didn't come out at baggage claim. I didn't want you to worry on our special day, so I used my backpack. Haru says, Oh! That's why you wore the same green sweater every day! Ms. Emma laughs. She says, Today, let's go to the Baggage Service desk at Brightwater Airport together. When your bag doesn't come, don't get upset. Just explain clearly and politely. My suitcase didn't arrive. Say it with me. My suitcase didn't arrive. Good! At the airport, a kind woman at the desk listens carefully. She asks, What does it look like? Ms. Emma says, It's big and blue, with a yellow ribbon on the handle. It has a name tag, too. The woman says, We're very sorry. Could you fill out this form, please? Let's read the form. "Baggage Service Form. Flight: 1120 from Skyport. Item: one large suitcase. Color: blue. Special marks: a yellow ribbon on the handle and a name tag. Inside: clothes, shoes, a hairbrush, and a travel guide. Please send the bag to the Seagull Hotel in Brightwater. We apologize for the trouble. We will call your hotel as soon as we find your bag." What color is the suitcase? Blue. What is on the handle? A yellow ribbon. That night, the phone in our room rings. Mr. Lee says, Good news! Your suitcase is here at the front desk! We all cheer. Now, phonics. Today's words end in ize, and they are all verbs. Apology, drop the y, add ize. Apologize. Real, add ize. Realize means suddenly know that something is true. Summary, drop the y, add ize. Summarize means tell the main points. Next time, our room gets very hot, and something is broken!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Could you give us a different room instead? We love our new room. But this morning, Ms. Emma is looking through her backpack. Then her jacket. Then her suitcase. She says calmly, Everyone, I can't find my passport. Your passports are safe in the travel pouch, but mine isn't there. Then she adds, Don't worry. When something is lost, the first thing to do is stay calm. If you ever lose something important on a trip, tell an adult right away. I'm the adult, so I'll ask at the front desk. I lost my passport. What should I do? Say it with me. I lost my passport. What should I do? Well done! We check all our bags together, and then we all go down to the lobby. Mr. Lee listens kindly and asks, Where did you last use it? Ms. Emma remembers. At the Baggage Service desk at the airport! I showed it there for the form. Mr. Lee says, I'll call the airport for you. While he calls, he gives us a card. Let's read the card. "Lost Your Passport? Don't panic. First, look carefully in your bags and pockets. Next, think about the last place you used it. Then, tell the hotel front desk. We can make phone calls for you. If you still cannot find it, an adult should go to the police and then contact their country's embassy. Children, always keep your passport with a grown-up you trust." Who should go to the embassy? An adult. Who should children keep their passports with? A grown-up they trust. Good news! The airport has it. It's safe at the Baggage Service desk. We all go to the airport with Ms. Emma and pick it up. Now, phonics. Memory, drop the y, add ize. Memorize. Sympathy, drop the y, add ize. Sympathize means understand how someone feels. lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Thank you for your help. That's very kind of you. Today, it's time to explore Brightwater! The sun is shining after yesterday's rain. Ms. Emma walks with us along the river, and Skye flies above us in her blue scarf. She calls down, Every trip is a story! Soon we reach Clock Tower Square. The tall Clock Tower stands in the middle, next to a fountain and a statue of a seagull. We want a picture of all of us together. Ms. Emma smiles at a kind woman with a map and says, Excuse me. Could you take our picture? The woman says, Of course! Say it with me. Excuse me. Could you take our picture? Great! Remember, we always ask with Ms. Emma right next to us. Let's read the sign in the square. "Welcome to Clock Tower Square. The Clock Tower was built more than two hundred years ago. Its bell rings every hour, from eight in the morning to eight at night. Please stay on the pavement and do not climb into the fountain. The underground station is across the bridge. Please join the queue at the ticket machines and check the timetable on the wall." When does the bell ring? Every hour, from eight in the morning to eight at night. Where is the underground station? Across the bridge. Just then, the bell rings. Bong, bong, bong! Click! The woman takes our picture at the perfect moment. Now, phonics. Today, we learn British and American words. Underground. In the UK, people say underground. In the US, people say subway. Sidewalk. In the US, people say sidewalk. In the UK, people say pavement. Queue. Q, u, e, u, e. It sounds just like the letter Q! In the US, people say line. Timetable. In the US, people say schedule. Both are correct English. Next time, we will go to the fish restaurant by the river and order lunch!

phonics.tipJa: ワールド34 の まとめ。Flight 205（two oh five。0 は oh と よむ）、visibility（visible ＝ 見える ＋ ity → 見とおし）、recommend（c は 1つ、m は 2つ）、memorize（memory の y を とって ＋ ize → おぼえる）、vacation（アメリカの ことば。CA を つよく。イギリスは holiday）。

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Would you mind helping us? Do you know where the check-in counter is? We're back! Our plane landed at the Airport of Wings, and today we're on the observation deck. Visibility is perfect, so we can see the white wing roof and the blue sea. It's time for the World 34 Travel Talk Show! Haru holds the microphone and tells the story of Flight 205. Riko talks about the City Museum, and Kiko shows her travel journal. Birimo shows everyone his Clock Tower keychain. Then Ms. Emma says, We learned so many polite words on this trip. Traveling is the best way to learn! Say it with me. Traveling is the best way to learn! Wonderful! Suddenly, Skye lands on the railing with a letter in her beak. Let's read the letter. "Dear friends of the Airport of Wings, Congratulations on finishing your trip! You asked politely, solved problems calmly, and thanked everyone you met. Now, children from many places are going to meet at the Hall of Wisdom. They will share ideas and talk together about our world. We would love you to join us. Please come with your teacher. Your new friends are waiting!" Where will the children meet? At the Hall of Wisdom. Who should come with the friends? Their teacher. Skye smiles and says, Congratulations! Here is your sixth stamp! Stamp! Then something amazing happens. The six stamps make a picture of a big building with a round roof. That's the Hall of Wisdom! Now, phonics. Let's review. Flight 205. Read it flight two oh five. Visibility. Visible means you can see it, so visibility means how far you can see. Recommend. One c and two m's. Memorize. Memory, drop the y, and add i, z, e. Vacation. In the US, people say vacation. In the UK, people say holiday. Goodbye, Skye! Thank you, Airport of Wings! See you at the Hall of Wisdom!
